arXiv:1311.7479v1 [math.AP] 29 Nov 2013

The blow-up rate for strongly perturbed semilinear wave equations

M. A. Hamza{\rm Hamza} Note: The first author is partially supported by the ERC Advanced Grant no.291214, BLOWDISOL during his visit to LAGA, Univ P13 in June 2013.    O. Saidi{\rm Saidi}
Abstract

We consider in this paper a large class of perturbed semilinear wave equation with subconformal power nonlinearity. In particular, we allow log perturbations of the main source. We derive a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables and use it to derive the blow-up rate. Throughout this work, we use some techniques developed for the unperturbed case studied by Merle and Zaag [12] together with ideas introduced by Hamza and Zaag in [5] for a class of weather perturbations.

Keywords: Semilinear wave equation, finite time blow-up, blow-up rate, perturbations.

MSC 2010 Classification: 35L05, 35B67, 35B20.

1 Introduction

This paper is devoted to the study of blow-up solutions for the following semilinear wave equation:

{∂t2u=Δ​u+|u|p−1​u+f⁡(u)+g⁡(x,t,∇u,∂tu)(u⁡(x,0),∂tu⁡(x,0))=(u0​(x),u1​(x))\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}^{2}u=\Delta u+|u|^{p-1}u+f(u)+g(x,t,\nabla u,\partial_{t}u)\\ (u(x,0),\partial_{t}u(x,0))=(u_{0}(x),u_{1}(x))\\ \end{array}\right. (1.1)

where u⁡(t):x∈ℝN→u⁡(x,t)∈ℝu(t):\,\,x\in{{\mathbb{R}}^{N}}\rightarrow u(x,t)\in{{\mathbb{R}}}, u0​(x)∈Hl​o​c,u1u_{0}(x)\in H^{1}_{loc,u} and u1​(x)∈Ll​o​c,u2u_{1}(x)\in L^{2}_{loc,u}. The space Ll​o​c,u2L^{2}_{loc,u} is the set of all v∈Ll​o​c2v\in L^{2}_{loc} such that

‖v‖Ll​o​c,u2≡supd∈ℝN(∫|x−d|<1|v⁡(x)|2​𝑑x)12<+∞,\|v\|_{L^{2}_{loc,u}}\equiv\sup_{d\in{{\mathbb{R}}^{N}}}(\int_{|x-d|<1}|v(x)|^{2}dx)^{\frac{1}{2}}<+\infty,

and the space Hl​o​c,u1={v∣v,|∇v|∈Ll​o​c,u2}.H^{1}_{loc,u}=\{v\mid v,|\nabla v|\in L^{2}_{loc,u}\}.
We assume that the functions ff and gg are 𝒞1{\cal{C}}^{1}, with f:ℝ→ℝf:{\mathbb{R}}\rightarrow{\mathbb{R}} and g:ℝ2​N+2→ℝg:{\mathbb{R}}^{2N+2}\rightarrow{\mathbb{R}} globally lipschitz, satisfying the following conditions:

(Hf)|f⁡(x)|≤M⁡(1+|x|p(log⁡(2+x2))a),for​all​x∈ℝwith⁡(M>0,a>1),(H_{f})\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,|f(x)|\leq M\Big(1+\frac{|x|^{p}}{(\log(2+x^{2}))^{a}}\Big),\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\rm for}\,\,{\rm all}\,x\in{\mathbb{R}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\rm with}\,(M>0,\,\,\,a>1),

Finally, we assume that

p>1​and​p<pc≡1+4N−1​if​N≥2.p>1\,\,{\rm and}\,\,p<p_{c}\equiv 1+\frac{4}{N-1}\,\,\,{\rm if}\,\,N\geq 2.

We can mention that Merle and Zaag [11], [12] and [13], studied the equation (1.1) with (f,g)≡(0,0)(f,g)\equiv(0,0) and 1<p≤pc1<p\leq p_{c}, later we give more details for this fact. Then in [5] and [6], Hamza and Zaag consider a similar class of perturbed equations, with (Hf)(H_{f}) and (Hg)(H_{g}) replaced by a more restrictive conditions: |f⁡(u)|≤M⁡(1+|u|q)|f(u)|\leq M(1+|u|^{q}) and |g⁡(u)|≤M⁡(1+|u|)|g(u)|\leq M(1+|u|) for some q​<p,M>​0.q<p,\,\,M>0. In this paper, we go beyond this restriction and allow stronger perturbations.

The Cauchy problem of equation (1.1) is wellposed in Hl​o​c,u1×Ll​o​c,u2H^{1}_{loc,u}\times L^{2}_{loc,u}. This follows from the finite speed of propagation and the wellposdness in H1×L2H^{1}\times L^{2}, valid whenever 1<p<1+4N−21<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}. The existence of blow-up solutions u⁡(t)u(t) of (1.1) follows from energy techniques (see for example Levine and Todorova [10], and Todorova [17]). Let N, p, a and M be fixed. Remark 1
  1. (i)

    Our method breaks down in the conformal case when p≡pcp\equiv p_{c}, since in the energy estimates in similarity variables, the perturbations terms are integrated on the whole unit ball, hence, difficult to control with the dissipation of the non perturbed equation (1.5), which degenerates to the boundary of the unit ball.

  2. (ii)

    The existence of this Lyapunov functional (and a blow-up criterion for equation (1.8) based in H⁡(w⁡(s),s)H(w(s),s), see Lemma 3.1 below) are a crucial step in the derivation of the blow-up rate for equation (1.1). Indeed, with the functional H⁡(w⁡(s),s)H(w(s),s) and some more work, as in [5] and [6] we are able to adapt the analysis performed in [12] for equation (1.5) and get the Theorem 2 below.

  3. (iii)

    It is worth noticing that the method breaks down when a≤1a\leq 1 too, because with some analysis to the Lyapunov functional we find an equality of type dd​s​(E⁡(w⁡(s))≤Csa​E​(w⁡(s))CLOSE\frac{d}{ds}(E(w(s))\leq\frac{C}{s^{a}}E(w(s)), EE is upper bounded if a>1a>1 but if a≤1a\leq 1 we can not conclude.

Remark 2

In a series of papers [11], [12], [13], [14], [15] and [16], Merle and Zaag give a full picture of the blow-up for solution of (1.5), in one space dimension and in dimension space N≥2N\geq 2.
The result of all this paper is extended by Hamza and Zaag for a class of perturbed problem in one space dimension or in higher dimension under radial symetry outside origin in [7], or in dimension space N≥2N\geq 2 in [5] and [6], (blow-up, profile, regularity of the blow-up graph, existence of characteristic points, etc…). Once again, we believe that the key point in the analysis of blow-up for equation (1.1) is the derivation of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables, which is the object of our paper.

As in [5], [6], [7], [11], [12], [13], [14], [15] and [16], the proof of Theorem 2 relies on four ideas (the existence of a Lyapunov functional, interpolation in Sobolev spaces, some Gagliardo-Nirenberg estimates and a covering technique adapted to the geometric shape of the blow-up surface). It happens that adapting the proof of [11], [12] and [13] given in the non-perturbed case (1.5) is straightforward, except for a key argument, where we bound the Lp+1L^{p+1} space-time norm of ww. Therefore, we only present that argument, and refer to [11], [12] and [13], for the rest of the proof.

This paper is divided in two sections, each of them devoted to the proof of a Theorem.

2 A Lyapunov functional for equation (1.8)

Throughout this section, we prove Theorem 1, we consider (w,∂sw)∈C([s0,+∞),ℋ)(w,\partial_{s}w)\in C([s_{0},\,\,+\infty),{\cal H}) where ww is a solution of (1.8) and s0∈ℝs_{0}\in{\mathbb{R}}. We aim at proving that the functional H⁡(w⁡(s),s)H(w(s),s) defined in (1.11) is a Lyapunov functional for equation (1.8), provided that s≥S1s\geq S_{1}, for some S1=S1​(N,p,M,a)S_{1}=S_{1}(N,p,M,a). We denote the unit ball of ℝN{\mathbb{R}}^{N} by BB. We denote by CC a constant which depends only on N,p,aN,p,a and on |B||B|.

3 Proof of Theorem 2

Throughout this section, we give a blow-up criterion in the w(y,s) variable and conclude the proof of Theorem 2.

There exists S2≥S1S_{2}\geq S_{1}, such that for all s0∈ℝs_{0}\in{{\mathbb{R}}} and ww solution of equation (1.8) defined to the right of s0s_{0}, such that ‖w‖Lp+1​(B)\|w\|_{L^{p+1}(B)} is locally bounded, if H⁡(w⁡(s3),s3)<0H(w(s_{3}),s_{3})<0 for some s3≥max⁡(S2,s0)s_{3}\geq\max(S_{2},s_{0}), then ww cannot be defined for all (y,s)∈B×[s3+1,+∞)(y,s)\in B\times[s_{3}+1,+\infty).

3.2 Boundedness of the solution in similarity variables

We prove Theorem 2 here. Note that the lower bound follows from the finite speed of propagation and wellposedness in H1×L2H^{1}\times L^{2}. For a detailed argument in the similar case of equation (1.5), see Lemma 3.1 (page 1136) in [12].
We consider uu a solution of (1.1) which is defined under the graph of x↦T⁡(x)x\mapsto T(x) and x0x_{0} is a non-characteristic point. Given some T0∈(0,T⁡(x0)]T_{0}\in(0,T(x_{0})], we introduce wx0,T0w_{x_{0},T_{0}} defined in (1.7), and write ww for simplicity, when there is no ambiguity. We aim at bounding ‖(w,∂sw)​(s)‖H1×L2\|(w,\partial_{s}w)(s)\|_{H^{1}\times L^{2}} for ss large.
As in [11], by combining Theorem 1 and Lemma 3.1 (use in particular the remark after that lemma) we get the following bounds:

Corollary 3.2

For all s≥s3^=S3^​(T0)=max⁡(S3,−log⁡(T0))s\geq\hat{s_{3}}=\hat{S_{3}}(T_{0})=\max(S_{3},-\log(T_{0})) , s2≥s1≥s3^s_{2}\geq s_{1}\geq\hat{s_{3}}, it holds that

−C≤E⁡(w⁡(s),s)≤M0.-C\leq E(w(s),s)\leq M_{0}.
∫s1s2∫B(∂sw)2​ρ1−|y|2​𝑑y​𝑑s≤M0.\int_{s_{1}}^{s_{2}}\int_{B}(\partial_{s}w)^{2}\frac{\rho}{1-|y|^{2}}dyds\leq M_{0}.

Starting from these bounds, the proof of Theorem 2 is similar to the proof in [11], [12] and [13]. To be more complete and in order to state our main result in a clear way, let us mention that the unique difference lays in the logarithmic term. In our opinion, handling these terms is straighforward in all the steps of the proof, except for the first step, where we bound the time averages of the Lρp+1​(B)L^{p+1}_{\rho}(B) norm of ww. For that reason, we only give that step and refer to [11], [12] and [13], for the remaining steps in the proof of Theorem 2. This is the step we prove here (in the following, K3K_{3} denotes a constant that depends on pp, NN, CC).

Proposition 3.3

For all s≥1+s3^s\geq 1+\hat{s_{3}};

∫ss+1∫B|w|p+1​ρ​𝑑y≤K3.\int_{s}^{s+1}\int_{B}|w|^{p+1}\rho dy\leq K_{3}.

Proof: The proof of Proposition 3.3 is the same as in Hamza and Zaag [5] and [6]. Exceptionally, the unique difference lays in the logarithmic term where we use the same technique as in the proof of Lemma 2.1 in Section 1. Since the derivation of Theorem 2 from Proposition 3.3 is the same as in the non-perturbed case treated in [11], [12] and [13], (up to some very minor changes), this concludes the proof of Theorem 2.
